answers.solution:
I diagnosed the class by building a real git reproduction (base commit → work commit with a clean post-commit index) and verified the fix. Environment note: `/workspace` only contained `problem.json`, so I created a self-contained, runnable solution.

## Deliverables (all in `/workspace/solution/`)

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `SOLUTION.md` | Full written solution (title, root cause, fix, verification) |
| `gitreins_judge_fix.py` | Python helpers: restage/patch/verdict/hang-doctrine |
| `restage_judge.sh` | Drop-in CLI: restage → `guard --full` |
| `verify.py` | Reproduces the defect and asserts the fix (exits 0) |

## Root cause (short)

- Tier1 derives "files to lint/test" from `git diff --cached` (index-vs-HEAD). **Before commit** that works; **after** commit/merge HEAD already contains the work, the index is clean, so tier1 returns `DEGRADED: lint/tests = no staged files`, and the combiner folds that into overall `FAIL`.
- The naive fix "just `git add` the work files" is a **no-op in a true post-merge checkout** (`HEAD == merged tree`). The fix must anchor to the recorded `BASE` SHA.
- Detached async jobs read their **own** cwd/index, so parent staging is invisible — the restage must run inside the job from a self-contained patch or the `BASE`/`WORK` SHAs.
- Tier2 criteria verification is valid; the empty-index tier1 `DEGRADED` is an artifact once the foreman `guard --full` is 5/5 (precedent `a8190eb` / `tick-249`).
- Hung async judges: timeout → retry once → close citing foreman evidence.

## The fix (core)

```bash
idx=$(mktemp -u "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gitreins-idx.XXXXXX"); trap 'rm -f "$idx"' EXIT
export GIT_INDEX_FILE="$idx"
git -C "$repo" read-tree "$base"                          # isolated index := BASE
mapfile -d '' f < <(git -C "$repo" diff --name-only -z "$base..$work")
git -C "$repo" add -A -- "${f[@]}"                        # -A stages deletions
git -C "$repo" diff --cached "$base" --stat              # tier1 targets vs BASE
guard --full                                              # tier1 evidence of record
```

Detached job: `git diff --binary "$base..$work" > work.patch`, then inside the job `read-tree "$base"` + `git apply --cached work.patch`. Verdict: `overall_verdict(tier1, tier2="COMPLETE", foreman_guard="PASS")` returns `COMPLETE` only when foreman evidence exists — otherwise it stays `FAIL` (no silent pass).

## Verification (actual `verify.py` output)

```
[1] tier1 DEGRADED reason='lint/tests = no staged files'; overall -> FAIL
[2] restage fix -> tier1 OK files=['README.md', 'calc.py', 'newmod.py']; real index clean
[3] DEGRADED + foreman PASS -> COMPLETE ("citing foreman guard --full"); no-foreman -> FAIL
[4] detached child buggy DEGRADED; patch-based restage -> OK
[5] hung judge bounded (1.00s), retry exhausted -> CLOSED citing foreman guard 5/5
ALL ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

Run: `cd /workspace/solution && python3 verify.py` (exit 0), and `./restage_judge.sh <repo> <base> <work> -- guard --full`.

The full markdown (with rollout checklist and close-out rule) is at `/workspace/solution/SOLUTION.md`.

signatures.description: A post-merge tier2 judge in chimera-v2 reads overall FAIL purely from its tier1 leg reporting DEGRADED (lint/tests = no staged files) even though the work is already committed and the merged tree passes guard --full 5/5. Root cause: the judge pipeline grades the git INDEX, which is empty post-commit; worse, for DETACHED async jobs even a pre-staged diff is useless because the job subprocess re-collects evidence from its own cwd/index state. Fix that worked (restage-then-judge, INT-GATE-001 class): git add the union of the work-commit files, run guard --full non-degraded as the tier1 evidence of record, then take the judge verdict for what it is - tier2 criteria-level verification is valid (COMPLETE with mutation-checked probes), tier1 DEGRADED is an artifact, cite the foreman guard run. Repo precedent: commit a8190eb and the tick-249 row notes. Also: async tier2 judges can HANG (4s CPU in 31min vs 7min for a healthy sibling) - doctrine is retry once, then close citing foreman evidence.
